LevelShift C2C Phase 1 Technical Specs V2.1 (tone/terminology rules mandated per agent)
positioning: For enterprise organizations navigating complex AI transformations, LevelShift is the single accountable partner that combines deep industry expertise, 500+ certified technical experts, and disciplined execution frameworks to help enterprises choose the right AI path — and succeed.
archetype: The Sage blended with the Ruler: trusted expert plus order, governance, and accountable outcomes.
tone: Positive, confident, respectful of senior readers. No urgency or fear framing. No overselling.

voice.label: Authoritative (Not Arrogant)
voice.do: Be direct. State your position. Back it with reasoning, data, or experience.
voice.dont: Lecture. Do not use 'clearly' or 'obviously', which can make the reader feel behind.

voice.label: Clear (Not Simplified)
voice.do: Use plain language for technical concepts. Define jargon the first time. Write shorter sentences.
voice.dont: Use buzzwords as shortcuts or oversimplify to the point of being misleading.

voice.label: Outcome-Driven (Not Feature-Focused)
voice.do: Lead with the business problem. Tie every capability to a measurable outcome.
voice.dont: List features without context or write about AI in the abstract.

voice.label: Industry-Grounded (Not Generic)
voice.do: Reference real industry challenges. Use sector-specific language where relevant.
voice.dont: Write content that could apply to any company or use vague phrases like 'businesses everywhere'.

wordChoice.bannedTermsNote: The playbook's banned-phrases section is a placeholder; this list stays empty until Marketing provides the real list. Overuse/avoid terms above are the only words the playbook names.
wordChoice.urgencyFearNote: Spec rule: no urgency/fear framing. Term list is a draft heuristic pending Marketing sign-off; the LLM prompt carries the rule in full.

terminology.rule: Business Central and F&O are strictly independent; never combine them in one campaign concept or claim.
Copilot is D365-cloud-only; never position Copilot for on-premise scenarios.

contentSelfCheck: Does the piece lead with a business problem or insight — not a product description?
Is every AI capability claim connected to a business outcome?
Would a senior enterprise leader feel respected reading this?
Have I removed all banned words and empty adjectives?
Is there at least one specific, concrete detail?
Does the piece represent a clear LevelShift point of view?
Is the call to action specific and single?
Could I read this aloud without it sounding like a brochure?

blog.purpose: Demonstrate that LevelShift understands the real problems enterprises face with AI adoption.
blog.structure: Intro/Hook (1–2 sentences) → The Problem → The Insight/Solution/Deep Dive (FAQs, infographic) → Practical Takeaway → CTA
blog.voice: First person plural (We). Confident and direct.

whitepaper.purpose: Serve readers who need to understand a challenge deeply before making an internal recommendation.
whitepaper.structure: Executive Summary → Context → Analysis: LevelShift framework → Practical Guidance → Appendix
whitepaper.voice: Third-person or authoritative first person. Data and evidence required.

service_page.purpose: Answer: can these people help me? Move the reader from interest to action.
service_page.structure: Opening: the business problem → What We Do → How We Work → Proof → CTA
service_page.voice: Second person (You). Every feature must be followed by a benefit.

case_study.purpose: Let results do the talking — the most powerful conversion asset at the Decision stage.
case_study.structure: Result at a glance → Client Context → The Problem → The LevelShift Approach → The Outcome (quantified) → Client Perspective
case_study.voice: Evidence-led. Past tense, active voice. Numbers over adjectives.

email.purpose: Move prospects through the buyer journey with relevance and timing.
email.structure: Subject line → Opening: one-sentence pain-point context → The Value → CTA: one clear action → Signature
email.voice: Personal and direct, one person to one person. Short paragraphs.

personas.title: The Transformation Mandate Owner (CDO / CTO / CIO, $1B+ revenue)
personas.pains: Fragmented AI initiatives with no enterprise coherence. Board pressure for measurable ROI.
personas.keyMessage: LevelShift is your single accountable AI transformation partner. We own the outcome from strategy to deployment.

personas.title: The Platform Architect (VP of IT / Enterprise Architect, mid-to-large enterprise)
personas.pains: Legacy systems creating integration debt. Teams stretched across Salesforce, Microsoft, and data platforms simultaneously.
personas.keyMessage: Technology-certified experts. Proven frameworks. Enterprise-grade implementation — with speed.

personas.title: The ROI Champion (CFO / COO / VP Finance, cost and efficiency focus)
personas.pains: High total cost of ownership on current platforms. Manual processes inflating overhead. Unclear ROI.
personas.keyMessage: LevelShift reduces total cost of ownership by up to 50% through AI-driven automation and right-sized managed services.

personas.title: The Revenue Accelerator (CRO / VP Sales / VP Operations, revenue cycle focus)
personas.pains: Revenue leakage from slow quote-to-cash. Disconnected CRM and ERP preventing real-time deal visibility.
personas.keyMessage: LevelShift accelerates your revenue cycle with faster quotes, smarter insights, measurable impact.

buyerJourney.trigger: Board mandate for AI. Competitive pressure. Failed internal initiative.
buyerJourney.content: Thought leadership blogs, AI trend reports, event keynotes, LinkedIn posts

buyerJourney.trigger: Evaluating partners. Building internal business case. RFP stage.
buyerJourney.content: Whitepapers, solution briefs, capability decks, webinars, practice pages, gated content

buyerJourney.trigger: Final vendor shortlist. Reference checks. Contract negotiation.
buyerJourney.content: Case studies, ROI calculators, executive briefings, demos, proposal decks

buyerJourney.trigger: Successful deployment. New business unit. Adjacent practice need.
buyerJourney.content: Success story assets, managed services proposals, upsell decks
